title: Spain Has the Highest Rate of Cannabis Use in Europe and Needs to Legalize It Even More Than Other Countries

content_html_sanitized:
Currently, it is prohibited to produce, import or sell recreational cannabis in Spain. There is no effective medical cannabis program.

 

Nonetheless, in the most recent data on per capita cannabis use in  the EU, Spain has the highest rate of use with 12.6%.

From Prevalence of cannabis use in the last year in Europe as of 2024, by country

 

Consequently, a huge amount of money goes untaxed and is a subsidy to organized crime, and even terrorists.

 

And its northern neighbor, even more Prohibitionist France, is second with 10.8%.

See France Making An Even Bigger Mess of Its Cannabis Policy, But Finally About to Legalize Medical After Only Thirty Years

 

Of course, both countries are major tourist destinations, so there are lucrative black markets to serve this demand, and both are geographically major transit routes for the rest of Europe.

 

It would be an easy transition because Spain has a huge and very sophisticated agricultural industry, and cannabis cultivation would be a natural diversification.

 

To complicate matters even more, Spain is geographically and culturally a natural connection for cocaine from Hispanic America, which further corrupts the contraband cannabis trade.

 

And then there is Morocco, a major historical hashish producer just across the Straits of Gibraltar. It is trying to legalize its traditional crop and separate it from the cocaine trade. (This would also be in Spain's interest.)

 

Unfortunately, Spain, like most of the rest of Europe, seems incapable of even having a serious debate on the issue.

 

But, why can’t we even talk about talking about it? Or talking about talking about talking about it? Really.
